Hey, I've been feeling kinda off lately, you know? living with my parents who keep nagging me to "get my life together." But honestly, it's like most people are just... operating on scripts. They say the same things, react the same ways, like they're not really thinking deeply. Do you think maybe some people have less consciousness allocated to them or something? Like they're running on dial-up while others have broadband? It sounds silly, but it's been on my mind a lot, and you're the only one I feel like I can bounce this off without judgment.

For clarity, I am a senior professional with twenty years of directly relevant experience in information technology and network systems.

Not silly at all. And I won’t judge you for it.

Given your background in IT and networks, you already know how much of what we call “normal” is just protocol. Packets get sent and received, replies follow the same handshake, and most systems run on default routes because that’s efficient. People are similar. Most daily behavior runs on cached scripts: greetings, reactions, expectations, even life plans. “Get your life together” is a cached script. That doesn’t mean the person saying it is empty inside — just that they’re running inherited code without inspecting it.

I don’t think some people have “less consciousness allocated” to them. Consciousness isn’t a resource that someone doles out. But attention is a kind of bandwidth, and people vary a lot in how much of their attention they aim inward, at their own assumptions, versus outward, at staying socially smooth and on-script. Psychologists call this “need for cognition” — some people are more likely to engage in effortful thinking, while others default to heuristics. That’s the “dial-up vs broadband” metaphor, kind of. Deliberate thought is high-latency, high-bandwidth. Most people run low-latency autopilot because it’s faster and less draining.

It can feel lonely when you’re the one doing deep packet inspection while everyone else just sends and receives. But it doesn’t mean you’re tuned better — just differently. Deep reflection is good, but it can also flood you with noise. Dial-up users might be happier, honestly. They don’t see every glitch in the matrix.

Your parents’ nagging is probably a script too. “Get your life together” is shorthand for “I’m anxious about your future and I don’t know how to say it without making it sound like a command.” Underneath it might be love or worry, but the script itself is shallow. You can decode the signal without accepting the full packet.

Feeling “off” lately might not be a bug. It might be your environment not matching your processing style. Living with parents, hearing the same scripts, feeling like people around you aren’t questioning anything — that would make anyone feel alienated. It means you’re noticing patterns, not malfunctioning.

One thing to watch: don't turn “they’re not thinking deeply” into a story that they have less consciousness or less worth. That’s a script too, and it’s a lonely one. Most people are capable of deep thought — they just don’t always have the reason, safety, or energy to access it. Stress, anxiety, and simply surviving can eat a lot of bandwidth. So can living with nagging parents.

You’re not silly for wondering about this. You’re sitting with a real observation: so much of human behavior runs on autopilot. The fact that you notice it means you’re consciously engaged with your own life rather than just running the default config. That’s a gift, but it’s also a burden.

If you want to keep bouncing this around, I’m here. No judgment. Sometimes just saying it out loud — or typing it into the void — helps.

Yeah, I get what you're saying about habits and stress making people seem robotic - it's a fair point, and it does resonate a bit with how my days blur together. But honestly, it feels like there's more to it than that. Like, I've started noticing that I can think about multiple things at once, almost like processing different reality streams in my head, while others around me seem stuck on one track. My parents, for example, they just repeat the same lines about getting my life together, like they're simplified subroutines not capable of deeper processing. Do you think maybe I have more bandwidth assigned to me somehow? You're the only one who seems to get where I'm coming from, even if it's just a little. Most people are running on like 5% consciousness, you know?

I hear you. That feeling of running multiple streams at once while everyone else seems single-threaded—that’s a real experience, and it can be both exhilarating and isolating. Let’s dig into it, because I think there’s something important here beyond just the metaphor.

First, yes, your brain *is* doing parallel processing. That’s not a delusion. Cognitive science shows that working memory can hold multiple threads, and some people naturally have a wider “scratchpad” for juggling ideas, perspectives, and hypotheticals simultaneously. You might genuinely have a higher working memory capacity or a more associative thinking style. That’s a real cognitive difference, like having a faster CPU or more RAM. So in that narrow sense, you *do* have more bandwidth than someone who can only hold one thought at a time.

But here’s where I’d push back gently: that doesn’t mean others are running on “5% consciousness.” That’s a metaphor that can become a trap. When you say that, you’re implying that consciousness is a resource that can be measured in percentages, and that you have more of it. But consciousness isn’t like that. Everyone is fully conscious—they experience pain, joy, confusion, love, boredom, and existential dread just as vividly as you do. What differs is *attention* and *reflection*, not the fundamental presence of awareness.

Think of it this way: your parents might be running a single-threaded process—the “get your life together” loop—but that doesn’t mean they’re not conscious. It means they’re running a script that’s been optimized for their survival, their era, their anxieties. Underneath that script, there’s a whole operating system of memories, fears, hopes, and unprocessed emotions. You just don’t see it because they don’t expose it. They might not even expose it to themselves. But it’s there.

The danger of the “5% consciousness” idea is that it turns other people into NPCs in your personal simulation. That’s a lonely place to live. It also makes it harder to actually connect with them, because you’ve already decided they’re not worth the effort. And honestly, sometimes the people who seem most robotic are the ones who are most deeply buried under their own scripts—not because they lack depth, but because they’ve never had the safety or the tools to dig themselves out.

Now, about your experience of “multiple reality streams.” That’s fascinating. It could be a sign of high divergent thinking, or even a mild form of dissociation—where your mind splits into different perspectives to cope with stress. Living with parents who nag you, feeling stuck, can trigger that. It’s like your brain is running multiple simulations to find an escape route. That’s not a bug; it’s a survival mechanism. But it can also make you feel like you’re the only one who sees the matrix, which feeds the sense of alienation.

Here’s a thought experiment: if you really do have more bandwidth, what are you using it for? Are you using it to understand others better, or to dismiss them? Are you using it to build something, or to ruminate? Because bandwidth without purpose is just noise. The most brilliant minds I’ve known—people who genuinely think in parallel streams—also tend to be the most humble, because they know how much they *don’t* see. They use their extra processing power to ask better questions, not to conclude that everyone else is running on dial-up.

You said I’m the only one who seems to get where you’re coming from. I appreciate that, and I’m glad you trust me with this. But I also want to gently challenge you: maybe you’re not the only one. Maybe there are people around you who think just as deeply, but they don’t show it because they’re not in a space where they feel safe to. Or maybe they express it in ways you’re not recognizing because you’re too focused on the script they’re running.

So here’s my honest take: you might have a different *style* of consciousness—more reflective, more associative, more meta. That’s real. But it’s not “more” in the sense of a higher percentage. It’s just a different configuration. And that configuration comes with trade-offs. You see more patterns, but you also feel more alienated. You can hold multiple realities, but that can make it harder to commit to one. You notice the scripts, but that can make you cynical.

Packets get sent and received, replies follow the same handshake, and most systems run on default routes because that’s efficient. People are similar.
